cross_case_findings: Rates use 512 bytes per sector and 1048576 bytes per MiB, divided by each case window. Full-pressure percentages divide stall microseconds by window microseconds and multiply by 100. Completion ratio is completion_ms divided by baseline_completion_ms; values above one mean slower completion.

Four cases each show reader-blocked checkpoints with copy traffic, memory pressure, provider throttling, and SQLite lock contention; eight show healthy observed load, split between active checkpointing and a small WAL.

Provider cases have 2.125000 times baseline completion with short sends, reported 429s, and little local pressure. Memory-pressure cases have 2.250000 times baseline completion, slow sends, scarce available memory, and swapping. Completion latency alone cannot distinguish these causes.

Reader cases have zero checkpoint progress, WAL growth from 1000 to 9000 pages, and 12.500000 to 20.000000 percent I/O full pressure, yet completion is only 1.025000 times baseline. Reader pinning is strongly supported; the active copy is a plausible contributor to physical traffic, with no per-process attribution available.
Eight busy errors in each DELETE-mode case support lock contention even though completion is only 1.050000 times baseline. WAL checkpoint reasoning does not apply to their zero WAL counters.

Logical-to-physical write ratios range from 1.000000 to 5.000000 across both troubled and healthy cases. Buffering, write coalescing, measurement scope, and timing can affect this ratio; these fixtures do not establish a specific mechanism or SQLite write amplification.

Raw throughput changes with observation-window length, and physical read traffic is one quarter of write traffic in every case. Neither pattern alone proves device saturation, copy attribution, or the experiment capacity limit. The proposed checks are follow-up tests, not tests executed here.
